chunks.content: Backend engineer who builds things that scale, now obsessed with AI.

Hi, my name is Peterson Ngo. I am based in Chicago, but exploring and trying to find a new city to explore. Outside of work, I am passionate about a few things: Video games, family, and sports/lifting.

I currently have 4+ YoE. My passion for Software Engineering came from playing video games growing up. From Pokemon on the Gameboy to Call Of Duty on the Xbox 360, I became super interested on how these games are developed and how a machine can interpret and connect people outside of the physical space. From there and building my first PC in 2016, I became obsessed with figuring out how things worked. I think this was the first introduction into backend development since backend is how the system works.
I am actively learning more about AI and integrating more of the AI tech stack into my repertoire — from agentic systems to LLM-powered workflows.

I keep things simple, ship fast, and iterate. Reliability over features. I believe the best engineers are the ones who can break down hard problems into clear, actionable steps and deliver real-world impact. I am not just here to write code — I am here to solve problems that matter.

I lead using the servant leadership model. As a leader, your job is to serve your team — remove blockers, mentor, and guide so they can do their best work. Leaders lead by example and set direction, but everyone on the team is on the same level with the same goal. I believe a rising tide lifts all boats. I have mentored 10+ engineers who have grown from junior to mid and senior levels.

I am incredibly driven. I want to work on hard problems that have real-world impact. I do not care about the company size or industry — I care about the challenge and the growth. One principle I have ingrained in my fiber: if you commit to anything, give 110% effort no matter what it is.
Open to the right opportunity. I am not actively searching, but I am always open to conversations about hard problems and impactful work.
